label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8)
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L); it never fires during the original or copy phases. Firing rate rises steeply with sequence length: ~0 for L<=5, 0.2% at L=6, 9% at L=7, 28% at L=8, 39% at L=9. L>=8 holds 86% of activations and 90% of the mass, and L=9 has slightly higher mean magnitude. Within long-sequence delimiter steps, whether it fires depends on token content in a distributed way. The first original token has the most effect: f, 1, z, e, x and 0 raise the rate up to ~5x, and sequences with more digits fire more often. Restricting to the high-lift first tokens raises precision to ~0.5 but costs recall (F1 0.50 vs 0.48), so the simpler length-only predicate is kept. Precision is only ~0.33, because most long-sequence delimiter steps stay inactive.
